name: My Favorite Spacetimes
description: A catalogue of exact solutions of Einstein's field equations. For each spacetime: its name, a description, tags, signature, the conventions shared by its charts and the spacetimes it is related to, each with its id, the kind of relation and why, and for each coordinate chart the coordinates, their domains, the parameters, the chart's own conventions, the line element, the nonzero metric components and the curvature invariants. Mathematics is LaTeX.
note: The catalogue page chooses a spacetime in the browser and has no address per spacetime, so page_url is the catalogue itself. data_url is the full record the page draws from: Christoffel symbols, Riemann, Ricci, Einstein and Weyl tensors, geodesic equations and the history with its references.

spacetimes.name: Aichelburg-Sexl Ultraboost
spacetimes.description: The gravitational field of a massless particle, the Schwarzschild field boosted to the speed of light with its energy held fixed. Spacetime is flat on either side of a single null plane, which carries an impulsive gravitational shock wave with the particle at its centre.
spacetimes.convention: We keep factors of $G$ and $c$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.

related.text: The Aichelburg-Sexl shock is a limit of Schwarzschild's field: the boost is taken to the speed of light with the energy held fixed, which flattens the field onto a null plane [aichelburg1971].
The family of waves with plane fronts and parallel rays that Heinrich Brinkmann found in 1925, to which the Aichelburg-Sexl shock belongs [brinkmann1925, bonnor1969light].
Flat spacetime on either side of the shock. Roger Penrose built such waves in 1972 by cutting Minkowski space along a null plane and joining the halves again with a warp [penrose1972impulsive].
A steady beam of light of finite width, whose exact field William Bonnor found in 1969. Outside the beam its profile is the shock's logarithm with no delta in front [bonnor1969light].
Another pp-wave whose profile is harmonic off a line. Here the line is the path of a massless particle, there a cosmic string carrying a wave [garfinkle1990].
The rotating black hole, boosted the same way. Valeria Ferrari and Paolo Pendenza took the limit along its axis in 1990 and found the field of massless particles on a ring [ferrari1990].

Two impulsive waves colliding, each with a plane front of the same strength everywhere, which focus each other onto a singularity [khan1971]. Two Aichelburg-Sexl shocks meeting head on close a trapped surface around the collision, as Penrose found in 1974 [eardley2002].
The counterparts of the pp-waves in anti-de Sitter space. Squeezed onto one front, a Siklos wave is the field of a null particle there [podolsky1998impulsive].
A black string moving around a small fifth dimension is a charged black hole to four dimensions. At the speed of light it is a wave of this kind in five dimensions [horowitz2012].

charts.name: Cartesian

parameters.description: Newton's gravitational constant
Energy of the massless source, the limit of $Mc^2/\sqrt{1 - V^2/c^2}$ as its rest mass $M$ goes to zero and its speed $V$ to $c$
An arbitrary length; changing it moves $v$ behind the shock by a constant, which is a change of coordinates

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $x$, $y$, and $z$ lengths, and $\delta$ is the Dirac delta, a prime on it a derivative with respect to its argument. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
charts.line_element: ds^2 = -c^2dt^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2 - \dfrac{4GE}{c^4}\ln\left(\dfrac{x^2 + y^2}{\rho_0^2}\right)\delta(ct - z)\left(c\,dt - dz\right)^2

charts.name: Null Cartesian

parameters.description: Newton's gravitational constant
Energy of the massless source, the limit of $Mc^2/\sqrt{1 - V^2/c^2}$ as its rest mass $M$ goes to zero and its speed $V$ to $c$
An arbitrary length; changing it moves $v$ behind the shock by a constant, which is a change of coordinates

charts.convention: We use the null coordinates $u = ct - z$ and $v = ct + z$, both lengths, with $x$ and $y$ the transverse lengths, and $\delta$ is the Dirac delta, a prime on it a derivative with respect to its argument. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

charts.name: Null Cylindrical

parameters.description: Newton's gravitational constant
Energy of the massless source, the limit of $Mc^2/\sqrt{1 - V^2/c^2}$ as its rest mass $M$ goes to zero and its speed $V$ to $c$
An arbitrary length; changing it moves $v$ behind the shock by a constant, which is a change of coordinates

charts.convention: We use the null coordinates $u = ct - z$ and $v = ct + z$, both lengths, with $\rho$ the distance from the axis of the source and $\phi$ the angle about it, and $\delta$ is the Dirac delta, a prime on it a derivative with respect to its argument. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

spacetimes.name: Alcubierre Warp Drive
spacetimes.description: A warp bubble metric that contracts space ahead of a ship and expands it behind, allowing travel that is effectively faster than light without locally exceeding light speed. It requires negative energy density (exotic matter) to sustain the bubble.

related.text: Warp drives with any shift vector $(u, v, w)$. José Natário found one in 2002 that neither expands nor contracts space anywhere [natario2002].

Alcubierre's bubble with a factor $B^2$ on its space, which hides a pocket 200 m across inside a bubble a few femtometres wide. That brings the negative energy down to a few solar masses [vandenbroeck1999].

A warp drive whose shift is the gradient of a potential, which Erik Lentz built in 2021 to have positive energy density for the observers riding with it [lentz2021]. Other observers still measure negative energy [santiago2022].

A second way to beat light with negative energy. A pilot inside an Alcubierre bubble cannot reach its wall to steer it, and Krasnikov's tube is laid down by a ship moving slower than light [krasnikov1998, everett1997].

The other way to cross space faster than light could in flat spacetime, a tunnel where Alcubierre has a bubble. Alcubierre set his drive beside it: "just as it happens with wormholes, exotic matter will be needed" [alcubierre1994].

A wormhole turned into a time machine by moving one of its mouths. Allen Everett showed in 1996 that a simple change to Alcubierre's bubble allows causal loops as well, as Alcubierre had conjectured [everett1996].
The drive switched off. With $v_s = 0$ the metric is Minkowski's, and with the bubble moving spacetime is still flat inside it and far from it [alcubierre1994].

charts.name: Cartesian

parameters.description: Bubble velocity in units of $c$, an arbitrary function of $t$ alone. The centre of the bubble follows the world line $x = x_s(t)$ with $dx_s/dt = c\,v_s(t)$, and nothing in the solution bounds it, so $v_s > 1$ is allowed and is the whole point of the construction: the ship rides at rest in its own flat patch and no local measurement ever catches it outrunning a light ray. The prime is the derivative along the chart coordinate, $v_s' = dv_s/d(ct)$, so it carries an inverse length.

Shape function, dimensionless, an arbitrary function of the four coordinates. It is $1$ at the centre of the bubble and $0$ far outside it, and the wall is wherever it falls between, so every derivative of $f$ is supported on the wall alone and the spacetime is flat everywhere else. Alcubierre's own choice is the radial profile $f(r_s)$ built from hyperbolic tangents, with $r_s = \sqrt{(x - x_s(t))^2 + y^2 + z^2}$ the distance from the centre of the bubble, but no component needs it. A profile that depends on $t$ and $x$ only through $x - x_s(t)$ obeys $\partial_t f = -v_s\,\partial_x f$ in this chart, and that is the one relation the components are not allowed to assume, since they are identities for an arbitrary $f$.

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $x$, $y$, and $z$ lengths. The velocity $v_s$ of the bubble is in units of $c$, so its centre follows $x = x_s(t)$ with $dx_s/dt = c\,v_s$, and the shape function $f$ is a dimensionless function of all four coordinates. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, where $\partial_t = c^{-1}\partial/\partial t$ and $v_s' = dv_s/d(ct)$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
charts.ricci_scalar: R = 2 v_s\,\partial_t\partial_x f + 2 v_s'\,\partial_x f + 2 v_s^2\,\left(\partial_x f\right)^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}v_s^2\,\left(\partial_y f\right)^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}v_s^2\,\left(\partial_z f\right)^2 + 2 v_s^2\,f\,\partial_x^2 f
charts.kretschmann: K = 4\left(v_s\,\partial_t\partial_x f + v_s'\,\partial_x f + v_s^2\left(\partial_x f\right)^2 + v_s^2 f\,\partial_x^2 f\right)^2 + 2\left(v_s\,\partial_t\partial_y f + v_s'\,\partial_y f + v_s^2 f\,\partial_x\partial_y f + 2v_s^2\,\partial_x f\,\partial_y f\right)^2 + 2\left(v_s\,\partial_t\partial_z f + v_s'\,\partial_z f + v_s^2 f\,\partial_x\partial_z f + 2v_s^2\,\partial_x f\,\partial_z f\right)^2 - 2v_s^2\left(\left(\partial_y f\right)^2 + \left(\partial_z f\right)^2\right)\left(v_s\,\partial_t\partial_x f + v_s'\,\partial_x f + v_s^2\left(\partial_x f\right)^2 + v_s^2 f\,\partial_x^2 f\right) + \dfrac{11}{4}v_s^4\left(\left(\partial_y f\right)^2 + \left(\partial_z f\right)^2\right)^2 - 2v_s^2\left(\left(\partial_x\partial_y f\right)^2 + \left(\partial_x\partial_z f\right)^2 + \left(\partial_y^2 f\right)^2 + \left(\partial_z^2 f\right)^2 + 2\left(\partial_y\partial_z f\right)^2\right)

spacetimes.name: Anti-de Sitter
spacetimes.description: The maximally symmetric vacuum solution with constant negative curvature, arising from a negative cosmological constant. Its conformal boundary underpins the AdS/CFT correspondence in theoretical physics.

related.text: A black hole placed in anti-de Sitter space. Stephen Hawking and Don Page showed in 1983 that a large one sits in stable equilibrium with its own radiation [hawking1983].
In three dimensions, anti-de Sitter space with its points identified by a discrete group of its symmetries is a black hole [banados1992, banados1993].
The same geometry with positive curvature, the vacuum of a positive cosmological constant. Its infinity is spacelike [hawking1973].
Anti-de Sitter space ironed flat, the limit $L \to \infty$.
Anti-de Sitter space maps conformally onto half of Einstein's static universe, and its infinity is the equator [hawking1973].
A product of anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions and a round sphere, held up by a uniform electromagnetic field [bertotti1959, robinson1959].
Anti-de Sitter space is a Malament-Hogarth spacetime, where one observer can see the whole endless future of another in a finite time of their own [hogarth1992].
Anti-de Sitter space with a rotating black hole put in. Henneaux and Teitelboim took it as the prototype for every isolated system in anti-de Sitter space [henneaux1985].
A vacuum with no cosmological constant that still carries an anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions along its axis, and a timelike boundary of its own [bardeen1999].

A rotating universe of dust built on anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions, with its metric stretched by $\sqrt{2}$ along a family of timelike lines and a flat direction added [godel1949]. Marianne Rooman and Philippe Spindel showed in 1998 that anti-de Sitter space is the boundary between such spaces that are causally safe and those with closed timelike curves [rooman1998].

Anti-de Sitter space sliced by hyperbolic planes has a horizon at $r = L$, and with points identified that horizon is a black hole's, of genus two or more [aminneborg1996]. Adding mass gives the family [mann1997].
Two pieces of anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions joined mirror to mirror along a flat wall, which keeps gravity four dimensional beside a fifth dimension of infinite size [randall1999b].
A bubble of anti-de Sitter space growing in a vacuum of higher energy. Seen from inside it is an open universe that falls back on itself after a time $\pi L/c$ [coleman1980].
Anti-de Sitter space with a gravitational wave crossing it. The profile $H$ of a pp-wave goes inside the bracket of the Poincaré patch, and at $H = 0$ the wave is gone [siklos1985, podolsky1998].
Anti-de Sitter space with a charged black hole put in. For the field theory on the boundary the charge is a charge density [chamblin1999].

Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity in five dimensions has an anti-de Sitter space among its solutions with no cosmological constant in its action. David Boulware and Stanley Deser found it in 1985 beside their black hole, and its graviton is a ghost [boulware1985, charmousis2008].

Anti-de Sitter space with one flat direction wound into a circle that shrinks to a point at a smooth tip, $r_0$ from the Poincaré horizon. It weighs less than anti-de Sitter space with the same circle [horowitz1998].
The Poincaré chart with time rescaled by a power of its own, $t \to \lambda^z t$ while $x \to \lambda x$. For $z > 1$ the Poincaré horizon turns into a null singularity [kachru2008, copsey2011].

Anti-de Sitter space with one term in $dt^2$ added along a null direction, which leaves of its symmetries those of the free Schrödinger equation. Dam Thanh Son proposed it in 2008 as the dual of cold atoms [son2008].

charts.name: Static global

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -3/L^2$; every sectional curvature of this spacetime is $-1/L^2$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

charts.name: Poincare patch

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, the same length as in the global chart, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$; the conformal boundary where the dual field theory lives is $z \to 0$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $x$, $y$, and $z$ lengths. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

spacetimes.name: Anti-de Sitter Soliton
spacetimes.description: A smooth spacetime of negative energy with no horizon: the planar black hole of anti-de Sitter space with its time and one flat direction exchanged, so that the horizon becomes a tip where a circle shrinks to a point. Gary Horowitz and Robert Myers found it in 1998 and conjectured that it is the ground state of its boundary conditions.
spacetimes.convention: The anti-de Sitter radius $L$ is a length. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.

related.text: The flat black hole of anti-de Sitter space, the black brane. Exchange its time with one flat direction and its horizon becomes the soliton's tip [horowitz1998].

At $r_0 = 0$ the line element is anti-de Sitter space's in its Poincaré patch, against which the soliton's negative energy is measured. In three dimensions the soliton is anti-de Sitter space itself [horowitz1998].

The black hole of three dimensions. Without rotation, and with its time and its angle exchanged, it is the soliton of three dimensions, which is anti-de Sitter space with no points identified [horowitz1998].

The round black hole of anti-de Sitter space, which trades places with anti-de Sitter space in Hawking and Page's phase transition. The flat black hole does the same with the soliton [hawking1983, surya2001].

charts.name: Horowitz-Myers

parameters.description: Radius of the tip, a length, where the circle $\tau$ shrinks to a point
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

charts.convention: We use Horowitz and Myers's coordinates $(t, r, \tau, x)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\tau$ and $x$ lengths, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The circle $\tau$ has period $\beta = 4\pi L^2/(3r_0)$, which makes the tip $r = r_0$ a regular point.

charts.name: Poincaré

parameters.description: Tip, a length, $z_0 = L^2/r_0$, where the circle $\tau$ shrinks to a point
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, z, \tau, x)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\tau$ and $x$ lengths, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The length $z = L^2/r$, with $r$ the radius of Horowitz and Myers's chart and $r_0$ its value at the tip, vanishes on the conformal boundary. The circle $\tau$ has period $\beta = 4\pi z_0/3$.

charts.name: Polar

parameters.description: Radius of the tip in Horowitz and Myers's chart, a length, which sets the scale of $t$ and $x$
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -3/L^2$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, \phi, x)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $x$ a length, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The proper distance $\rho$ from the tip is set by $r^3 = r_0^3\cosh^2(3\rho/2L)$, with $r$ the radius of Horowitz and Myers's chart, and $\phi = 2\pi\tau/\beta$ is the angle around the circle $\tau$ of period $\beta = 4\pi L^2/(3r_0)$.

charts.name: Five Dimensions

parameters.description: Radius of the tip, a length, where the circle $\tau$ shrinks to a point
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -6/L^2$

charts.convention: We use Horowitz and Myers's coordinates $(t, r, \tau, x, y)$ in five dimensions, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\tau$, $x$, and $y$ lengths, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The circle $\tau$ has period $\beta = \pi L^2/r_0$, which makes the tip $r = r_0$ a regular point.

charts.name: Three Dimensions

parameters.description: Radius of the tip, a length, where the circle $\tau$ shrinks to a point
Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, with $\Lambda = -1/L^2$

charts.convention: We use Horowitz and Myers's coordinates $(t, r, \tau)$ in three dimensions, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\tau$ a length, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The circle $\tau$ has period $\beta = 2\pi L^2/r_0$, which makes the tip $r = r_0$ a regular point.

spacetimes.name: Black Hole Threaded by a Cosmic String
spacetimes.description: A Schwarzschild black hole with a straight cosmic string through it. Off the axis it is Schwarzschild's vacuum, and around the whole axis, horizon included, a wedge is missing whose angle the string's tension sets, which lowers the horizon's area and the black hole's energy at a fixed mass.
spacetimes.convention: The Schwarzschild radius is $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, and $b = 1 - 4G\mu/c^2$ for a string of mass per unit length $\mu$, so the deficit angle is $2\pi(1 - b) = 8\pi G\mu/c^2$. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.

related.text: The black hole with the string pulled out, $b = 1$, where the missing wedge closes.
The string with the black hole taken out, $r_s = 0$, which leaves a flat cone.
A black hole with a string on one side alone. That string pulls it into uniform acceleration [kinnersley1970, achucarro1995].
The rotating black hole. A string through it leaves a cone as well, measured in a frame that turns with the hole, as Ruth Gregory, David Kubizňák, and Danielle Wills found in 2013 [gregory2013].

charts.name: Static

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, with $M$ the gravitational mass
$b = 1 - 4G\mu/c^2$, with $\mu$ the string's mass per unit length, equal to its tension, $0 < b \le 1$; the deficit angle is $2\pi(1 - b)$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$, the deficit carried by $g_{\phi\phi} = b^2r^2\sin^2\theta$.

charts.name: Static with the Wedge Removed

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, with $M$ the gravitational mass
$b = 1 - 4G\mu/c^2$, with $\mu$ the string's mass per unit length, equal to its tension, $0 < b \le 1$; the deficit angle is $2\pi(1 - b)$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \tilde\phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\tilde\phi = b\phi$ periodic in $2\pi b$, so that the line element is Schwarzschild's.

charts.name: Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, with $M$ the gravitational mass
$b = 1 - 4G\mu/c^2$, with $\mu$ the string's mass per unit length, equal to its tension, $0 < b \le 1$; the deficit angle is $2\pi(1 - b)$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \phi)$, with the retarded time $u = ct - r - r_s\ln\left|r/r_s - 1\right|$ a length and $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$.

charts.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, with $M$ the gravitational mass
$b = 1 - 4G\mu/c^2$, with $\mu$ the string's mass per unit length, equal to its tension, $0 < b \le 1$; the deficit angle is $2\pi(1 - b)$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, with the advanced time $v = ct + r + r_s\ln\left|r/r_s - 1\right|$ a length and $\phi$ periodic in $2\pi$.

spacetimes.name: Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli Black Hole
spacetimes.description: A rotating black hole in three spacetime dimensions with a negative cosmological constant. It has constant negative curvature everywhere, being anti-de Sitter space with points identified by a discrete boost, and it carries a temperature and an entropy that can be computed exactly.
spacetimes.convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, with $M = 8Gm/c^2$ and $J = 8Gj/c^3$ for a hole of mass $m$ and angular momentum $j$, and $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions. We write $N^2 = r^2/\ell^2 - M + J^2/(4r^2)$, which vanishes on the horizons $r_\pm^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}M\ell^2\left(1 \pm \sqrt{1 - J^2/(M^2\ell^2)}\right)$.

related.text: The rotating black hole of four dimensions. The BTZ black hole has an outer and an inner horizon as Kerr's does, in a spacetime of constant curvature [banados1992].
The black hole of anti-de Sitter space in four dimensions, which has a curvature singularity at its centre.

The BTZ black hole is anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions with its points identified, so it is locally anti-de Sitter space everywhere. At $M = -1$ and $J = 0$ it is anti-de Sitter space [banados1992, banados1993].
Minkowski space identified under a boost, as the BTZ black hole is anti-de Sitter space identified under one [misner1967, banados1993].

Sören Holst and Hans-Jürgen Matschull showed in 1999 that two massless particles colliding in anti-de Sitter space make a Gott universe, which, with its closed timelike curves treated as singular, is a rotating BTZ black hole [holst1999].

The spinning point particle of gravity in three dimensions with no cosmological constant, drawn out along a line into a string. It has no horizon, and its closed timelike curves lie close to the source [deser1984, deser1992time].
The rotating black hole of anti-de Sitter space in four dimensions. Its boundary is a rotating Einstein universe too, one dimension up [hawking1999rotation].

Schwarzschild's metric with a constant $\lambda^2$ added to $-g_{tt}$, a wormhole that passes for a black hole. Sergey Solodukhin made that change first in the BTZ black hole, in 2005, to restore unitarity [solodukhin2005, damour2007].

Dust collapsing to a black hole in four dimensions. Robert Mann and Simon Ross carried the collapse over to three in 1993, where dust falling under a negative cosmological constant ends as a BTZ black hole [mann1993].
The same identification of points carried to four dimensions, where the horizon comes out a torus or a surface of genus two or more [aminneborg1996].
A black hole in two dimensions, found in string theory. Times a circle, it is the string dual of the BTZ hole without rotation [horowitz1993].

With no cosmological constant a mass in three dimensions makes a cone and no black hole. Hans-Jürgen Matschull collided two such particles in anti-de Sitter space in 1999 and got this black hole [deser1984, matschull1999].
Kaigorodov's wave in anti-de Sitter space of four dimensions has a version in three, and it is the extreme BTZ black hole [cvetic1999].

A charged hole in four dimensions crossed by two streams of radiation, whose mass function grows without limit at its inner horizon [poisson1989]. The charged spinning hole in three dimensions does the same [chan1996].
The hole without rotation with its time and its angle exchanged. In three dimensions that is anti-de Sitter space itself, and in four or more a smooth spacetime of negative energy [horowitz1998].

charts.name: Stationary

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$
Mass, dimensionless, $M = 8Gm/c^2$ for a hole of mass $m$, with $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions
Angular momentum, a length, $J = 8Gj/c^3$ for a hole of angular momentum $j$; a horizon exists only for $|J| \le M\ell$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

charts.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$
Mass, dimensionless, $M = 8Gm/c^2$ for a hole of mass $m$, with $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions
Angular momentum, a length, $J = 8Gj/c^3$ for a hole of angular momentum $j$; a horizon exists only for $|J| \le M\ell$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \tilde\phi)$, with the advanced time $v$ a length, $dv = c\,dt + dr/N^2$ and $d\tilde\phi = d\phi + J\,dr/(2r^2N^2)$.

charts.name: Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Anti-de Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant through $\Lambda = -1/\ell^2$
Mass, dimensionless, $M = 8Gm/c^2$ for a hole of mass $m$, with $G$ Newton's constant in three dimensions
Angular momentum, a length, $J = 8Gj/c^3$ for a hole of angular momentum $j$; a horizon exists only for $|J| \le M\ell$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(u, r, \tilde\phi)$, with the retarded time $u$ a length, $du = c\,dt - dr/N^2$ and $d\tilde\phi = d\phi - J\,dr/(2r^2N^2)$.

spacetimes.name: Bardeen Regular Black Hole
spacetimes.description: A black hole with horizons and no singularity, which James Bardeen proposed in 1968. A ball of de Sitter space sits where Schwarzschild's singularity would be, and Eloy Ayón-Beato and Alberto García showed in 2000 that the field of a magnetic monopole in a nonlinear electrodynamics is its source.
spacetimes.convention: The Schwarzschild radius is $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, and the length $g$ is the charge of the magnetic monopole. We keep factors of $c$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.

related.text: Bardeen took this charged black hole for inspiration. The two share a tower of exteriors and interiors, and Bardeen's has a regular centre where Reissner-Nordström's has a timelike singularity [borde1994, ayonbeato2000].
Bardeen's black hole with the monopole switched off. At $g = 0$ the metric function is Schwarzschild's $1 - r_s/r$, and the singularity is back.

The core of Bardeen's black hole. Near the centre $f \approx 1 - r_sr^2/g^3$, de Sitter's static metric with $\Lambda = 3r_s/g^3$, and in the limit $g \to \infty$ at fixed $r_s/g^3$ the whole metric is de Sitter's [ansoldi2008].
Another black hole with no singularity. Where Bardeen's has a regular centre, Simpson and Visser's has a throat of radius $a$, and its inside bounces into another universe [simpson2019].
A regular black hole of the same kind whose metric function is a ratio of polynomials. Sean Hayward let its mass change in time in 2006, so that it forms and evaporates [hayward2006].
Gliner's vacuum with $p = -\rho$ as the whole interior of a collapsed star, held under a thin shell with no horizon [mazur2004, gliner1966].

Ori's model of a charged hole with radiation crossing it, whose mass function grows without limit at the inner horizon. Carried over to Bardeen's metric it gives an exponentially growing mass at the inner horizon as well [carballorubio2021].

charts.name: Static Spherical

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$

Charge of the magnetic monopole, a length. The black hole has two horizons for $g < 2r_s/3\sqrt{3}$, with $r_\pm$ their radii and $\kappa_\pm$ their surface gravities, one for $g = 2r_s/3\sqrt{3}$, and none beyond

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

charts.name: Outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$

Charge of the magnetic monopole, a length. The black hole has two horizons for $g < 2r_s/3\sqrt{3}$, with $r_\pm$ their radii and $\kappa_\pm$ their surface gravities, one for $g = 2r_s/3\sqrt{3}$, and none beyond

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(u, r, \theta, \phi)$, with the retarded time $u = ct - r_*$ a length, where $dr_*/dr = \left(1 - r_s r^2/\left(r^2 + g^2\right)^{3/2}\right)^{-1}$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$.

charts.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$

Charge of the magnetic monopole, a length. The black hole has two horizons for $g < 2r_s/3\sqrt{3}$, with $r_\pm$ their radii and $\kappa_\pm$ their surface gravities, one for $g = 2r_s/3\sqrt{3}$, and none beyond

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \theta, \phi)$, with the advanced time $v = ct + r_*$ a length, where $dr_*/dr = \left(1 - r_s r^2/\left(r^2 + g^2\right)^{3/2}\right)^{-1}$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$.

spacetimes.name: Bartnik-McKinnon Soliton
spacetimes.description: A static ball of SU(2) Yang-Mills field held together by its own gravity, with a regular centre, no horizon, and flat space far away. Neither a Yang-Mills field nor gravity makes such a ball alone. No formula is known for it: the solutions are found by numerical integration, one for each number of zeros of the field, and every one of them is unstable.
spacetimes.convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.

related.text: The solitons' outside in the limit of infinitely many zeros. As $n \to \infty$ the metric beyond $r = \ell$ tends to the extreme Reissner-Nordström black hole of a magnetic monopole, $1 - 2m/r \to (1 - \ell/r)^2$ [breitenlohner1994, volkov1999].

The solitons' edge in the same limit. As $n \to \infty$ the sphere $r = \ell$ recedes to an infinite distance from the centre, and the metric near it tends to the product of a pseudosphere and a sphere of radius $\ell$ [breitenlohner1994].

The other ball of field held together by its own gravity and known only numerically, made of a massive scalar field with a turning phase. Boson stars up to the heaviest are stable, and every one of these solitons is unstable [gleiser1989, lee1989, volkov1999].

The static sphere with both of its functions free, $e^{2\Phi} = \sigma^2(1 - 2m/r)$. A star fills it with fluid; the soliton fills it with a Yang-Mills field, whose stress along the radius differs from its stress across it.

The soliton's far field, and one of its two fates. Far from the centre the metric approaches Schwarzschild's of the soliton's mass, and a perturbed soliton either collapses to a Schwarzschild black hole or explodes [bartnik1988, zhou1991].
Another static ball with no surface, whose stress along the radius differs from its stress across it. Einstein made his of particles on circular orbits, and it can be written in closed form.

Collapse at the threshold, with a scalar field. Roberts's solution looks the same at every scale, as the critical solution does on one of the two thresholds Choptuik, Chmaj, and Bizoń found for a Yang-Mills field; on the other the critical solution is the first soliton [choptuik1996].

charts.name: Areal Radius

parameters.description: Lapse function, dimensionless: a clock held at radius $r$ runs at $\sigma\sqrt{1 - 2m/r}$ of the rate $t$ counts. On a solution $\partial_r\sigma = 2\ell^2\sigma\left(\partial_r w\right)^2/r$, and $\sigma \to 1$ far away fixes the constant it would otherwise carry

Mass function, a length: $m = GM(r)/c^2$ with $M(r)$ the mass inside the sphere of radius $r$, and $m(0) = 0$. On a solution $\partial_r m = \ell^2\left(1 - 2m/r\right)\left(\partial_r w\right)^2 + \ell^2\left(1 - w^2\right)^2/(2r^2)$, the energy of the Yang-Mills field in each shell

Amplitude of the Yang-Mills field, dimensionless: the SU(2) potential is purely magnetic, with $w = \pm 1$ where there is no field and $w = 0$ in the field of a magnetic monopole. On a solution $r^2\left(1 - 2m/r\right)\partial_r^2 w + \left(2m - \ell^2\left(1 - w^2\right)^2/r\right)\partial_r w + w\left(1 - w^2\right) = 0$. A solution regular at the centre and flat far away exists for one starting value $b$ in $w = 1 - br^2/\ell^2 + \dots$ for each number $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$ of zeros of $w$, and is known only numerically

The one length of the theory, $\ell = \sqrt{4\pi G}/(gc^2)$ with $g$ the coupling constant of the Yang-Mills field, so that masses come in units of $c^2\ell/G$. The soliton with one zero has $b = 0.4537$ and the mass $0.8286\,c^2\ell/G$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius. The mass function $m(r)$ and the unit $\ell$ are lengths, the lapse function $\sigma(r)$ and the amplitude $w(r)$ of the Yang-Mills field are dimensionless, and we leave the three functions free, since no solution is known in closed form. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
charts.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{\left(2r^2\left(r - 2m\right)\partial_r^2\sigma - 6r\left(r\,\partial_r m - m\right)\partial_r\sigma - 2\sigma\left(r^2\,\partial_r^2 m - 2r\,\partial_r m + 2m\right)\right)^2}{r^6\sigma^2} + \dfrac{2\left(2r\left(r - 2m\right)\partial_r\sigma - 2\sigma\left(r\,\partial_r m - m\right)\right)^2}{r^6\sigma^2} + \dfrac{8\left(r\,\partial_r m - m\right)^2}{r^6} + \dfrac{16m^2}{r^6}

charts.name: Isotropic

parameters.description: Dimensionless: a clock held at $\rho$ runs at $\sqrt{f}$ of the rate $t$ counts, and $f \to 1$ far away. In the functions of the areal radius it is $\sigma^2\left(1 - 2m/r\right)$ on the same sphere
Dimensionless, with $h/f$ the factor that multiplies flat space: the sphere of isotropic radius $\rho$ has the areal radius $r = \rho\sqrt{h/f}$, and $h \to 1$ far away

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \rho, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\rho$ the isotropic radius, a length, in which space is conformally flat. The functions $f(\rho)$ and $h(\rho)$ are dimensionless and left free, the areal radius is $r = \rho\sqrt{h/f}$, and $d\rho/\rho = dr/(r\sqrt{1 - 2m/r})$ for the mass function $m$, with $\rho/r \to 1$ far away. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
charts.ricci_scalar: R = \dfrac{2\rho\,f\,h^2\,\partial_\rho^2 f - 4\rho\,f^2\,h\,\partial_\rho^2 h - 3\rho\,h^2\left(\partial_\rho f\right)^2 + \rho\,f\,h\,\partial_\rho f\,\partial_\rho h + 4f\,h^2\,\partial_\rho f + 3\rho\,f^2\left(\partial_\rho h\right)^2 - 8f^2\,h\,\partial_\rho h}{2\rho\,f\,h^3}
charts.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{12\rho^2\,f^2\,h^4\left(\partial_\rho^2 f\right)^2 - 16\rho^2\,f^3\,h^3\,\partial_\rho^2 f\,\partial_\rho^2 h - 16\rho^2\,f\,h^4\left(\partial_\rho f\right)^2\,\partial_\rho^2 f - 4\rho^2\,f^2\,h^3\,\partial_\rho f\,\partial_\rho h\,\partial_\rho^2 f + 16\rho\,f^2\,h^4\,\partial_\rho f\,\partial_\rho^2 f + 16\rho^2\,f^3\,h^2\left(\partial_\rho h\right)^2\,\partial_\rho^2 f - 16\rho\,f^3\,h^3\,\partial_\rho h\,\partial_\rho^2 f + 8\rho^2\,f^4\,h^2\left(\partial_\rho^2 h\right)^2 + 16\rho^2\,f^2\,h^3\left(\partial_\rho f\right)^2\,\partial_\rho^2 h - 16\rho\,f^3\,h^3\,\partial_\rho f\,\partial_\rho^2 h - 16\rho^2\,f^4\,h\left(\partial_\rho h\right)^2\,\partial_\rho^2 h + 16\rho\,f^4\,h^2\,\partial_\rho h\,\partial_\rho^2 h + 11\rho^2\,h^4\left(\partial_\rho f\right)^4 - 8\rho^2\,f\,h^3\left(\partial_\rho f\right)^3\,\partial_\rho h - 32\rho\,f\,h^4\left(\partial_\rho f\right)^3 - 7\rho^2\,f^2\,h^2\left(\partial_\rho f\right)^2\left(\partial_\rho h\right)^2 + 48\rho\,f^2\,h^3\left(\partial_\rho f\right)^2\,\partial_\rho h + 32f^2\,h^4\left(\partial_\rho f\right)^2 - 4\rho^2\,f^3\,h\,\partial_\rho f\left(\partial_\rho h\right)^3 - 8\rho\,f^3\,h^2\,\partial_\rho f\left(\partial_\rho h\right)^2 - 48f^3\,h^3\,\partial_\rho f\,\partial_\rho h + 9\rho^2\,f^4\left(\partial_\rho h\right)^4 - 8\rho\,f^4\,h\left(\partial_\rho h\right)^3 + 24f^4\,h^2\left(\partial_\rho h\right)^2}{4\rho^2\,f^2\,h^6}

charts.name: Tortoise

parameters.description: Dimensionless, the factor that multiplies the flat plane of $t$ and $\xi$: a clock held at $\xi$ runs at $\sqrt{F}$ of the rate $t$ counts, and $F \to 1$ far away. In the functions of the areal radius it is $\sigma^2 N$ on the same sphere
Areal radius of the sphere at $\xi$, a length, with $r(0) = 0$ and $\partial_\xi r = \sigma N$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \xi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\xi$ the tortoise coordinate, a length measured from the centre, with $d\xi/dr = 1/(\sigma N)$ for the areal radius $r$, the lapse function $\sigma$, and $N = 1 - 2m/r$ with $m$ the mass function. The function $F(\xi)$ is dimensionless, $r(\xi)$ is a length, and we leave both free. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
charts.ricci_scalar: R = \dfrac{2F^3 - 2F^2\left(\partial_\xi r\right)^2 + r^2\left(\partial_\xi F\right)^2 - 4F^2\,r\,\partial_\xi^2 r - F\,r^2\,\partial_\xi^2 F}{F^3\,r^2}
charts.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{F^2\,r^4\left(\partial_\xi^2 F\right)^2 - 2F\,r^4\left(\partial_\xi F\right)^2\,\partial_\xi^2 F + 8F^4\,r^2\left(\partial_\xi^2 r\right)^2 - 8F^3\,r^2\,\partial_\xi F\,\partial_\xi r\,\partial_\xi^2 r + r^4\left(\partial_\xi F\right)^4 + 4F^2\,r^2\left(\partial_\xi F\right)^2\left(\partial_\xi r\right)^2 + 4F^4\left(\partial_\xi r\right)^4 - 8F^5\left(\partial_\xi r\right)^2 + 4F^6}{F^6\,r^4}

charts.name: Breitenlohner-Forgács-Maison

parameters.description: Dimensionless, with $A \to 1$ far away: the lapse function of the areal radius, there written $\sigma$, on the same sphere
Dimensionless, $N = \sqrt{1 - 2m/r}$ with $m$ the mass function, a length: a clock held at $\tau$ runs at $AN$ of the rate $t$ counts, and $N = 1$ at the centre and far away
Areal radius of the sphere at $\tau$, a length, with $\partial_\tau r = rN$, so that $r$ grows as $e^\tau$ near the centre and far away

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, \tau, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $\tau$ dimensionless, defined by $\partial_\tau r = rN$ for the areal radius $r$, so that $\tau \to -\infty$ at the centre. The functions $A(\tau)$ and $N(\tau)$ are dimensionless, $r(\tau)$ is a length, and we leave the three free. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
charts.ricci_scalar: R = \dfrac{2A\,N\,r^2 + 2A\,N\left(\partial_\tau r\right)^2 - 2A\,r\,\partial_\tau N\,\partial_\tau r - 2N\,r\,\partial_\tau A\,\partial_\tau r - 4r^2\,\partial_\tau A\,\partial_\tau N - 4A\,N\,r\,\partial_\tau^2 r - 2A\,r^2\,\partial_\tau^2 N - 2N\,r^2\,\partial_\tau^2 A}{A\,N\,r^4}
charts.kretschmann: K = \dfrac{4N^2\,r^4\left(\partial_\tau^2 A\right)^2 + 8A\,N\,r^4\,\partial_\tau^2 A\,\partial_\tau^2 N + 16N\,r^4\,\partial_\tau A\,\partial_\tau N\,\partial_\tau^2 A - 8N^2\,r^3\,\partial_\tau A\,\partial_\tau r\,\partial_\tau^2 A - 8A\,N\,r^3\,\partial_\tau N\,\partial_\tau r\,\partial_\tau^2 A + 4A^2\,r^4\left(\partial_\tau^2 N\right)^2 + 16A\,r^4\,\partial_\tau A\,\partial_\tau N\,\partial_\tau^2 N - 8A\,N\,r^3\,\partial_\tau A\,\partial_\tau r\,\partial_\tau^2 N - 8A^2\,r^3\,\partial_\tau N\,\partial_\tau r\,\partial_\tau^2 N + 8A^2\,N^2\,r^2\left(\partial_\tau^2 r\right)^2 - 16A^2\,N^2\,r\left(\partial_\tau r\right)^2\,\partial_\tau^2 r + 16r^4\left(\partial_\tau A\right)^2\left(\partial_\tau N\right)^2 - 16N\,r^3\left(\partial_\tau A\right)^2\,\partial_\tau N\,\partial_\tau r + 12N^2\,r^2\left(\partial_\tau A\right)^2\left(\partial_\tau r\right)^2 - 16A\,r^3\,\partial_\tau A\left(\partial_\tau N\right)^2\,\partial_\tau r + 24A\,N\,r^2\,\partial_\tau A\,\partial_\tau N\left(\partial_\tau r\right)^2 + 12A^2\,r^2\left(\partial_\tau N\right)^2\left(\partial_\tau r\right)^2 + 12A^2\,N^2\left(\partial_\tau r\right)^4 - 8A^2\,N^2\,r^2\left(\partial_\tau r\right)^2 + 4A^2\,N^2\,r^4}{A^2\,N^2\,r^8}

spacetimes.name: Bell-Szekeres Colliding Electromagnetic Waves
spacetimes.description: Two plane electromagnetic shock waves colliding head on in flat space. Where both have passed the spacetime is locally the Bertotti-Robinson universe, and the waves focus each other onto a Killing-Cauchy horizon with the curvature finite everywhere.
spacetimes.convention: No coordinate carries dimensions of time, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.

related.text: Where both waves have passed, the metric is that of the Bertotti-Robinson universe in other coordinates, with $1/\sqrt{2ab}$ for the radius of both factors and $x$ running along its circle of longitude without closing [griffiths1991, feinstein1995].

Khan and Penrose collide two impulsive gravitational waves in the same four regions, flat space, one wave, the other wave, and both, and their waves focus each other onto a curvature singularity [khan1971, griffiths1991].

Behind either wave alone the spacetime is a plane electromagnetic wave, the pp-wave with $H = -a^2\Theta(u)(x^2 + y^2)$ in Brinkmann's coordinates, which Bell and Szekeres's chart writes as $-2\,du\,dv + \cos^2(au)(dx^2 + dy^2)$ [griffiths1991].
Ahead of both waves, where $u < 0$ and $v < 0$, the spacetime is flat [griffiths1991].
Peter Szekeres's other spacetime, dust cosmologies with no symmetry, from the year after this one [szekeres1975].

charts.name: Double Null

parameters.description: Strength of the wave that crosses $u = 0$, an inverse length: behind that wave alone the null rays across its front meet at $u = \pi/(2a)$
Strength of the wave that crosses $v = 0$, an inverse length: behind that wave alone the null rays across its front meet at $v = \pi/(2b)$

charts.convention: We use null coordinates $(u, v, x, y)$ where both waves have passed, all four of them lengths, with $x$ and $y$ across the wave fronts. Ahead of one wave or both, where $u < 0$ or $v < 0$, the metric is this one with $u$ or $v$ set to zero.

charts.name: Time and Space

parameters.description: Strength of the wave that crosses $u = 0$, an inverse length
Strength of the wave that crosses $v = 0$, an inverse length; $1/\sqrt{2ab}$ is the radius of both factors of the product AdS$_2 \times$ S$^2$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(\xi, \eta, x, y)$ where both waves have passed, with $\xi = au + bv$ and $\eta = bv - au$ dimensionless, and $x$ and $y$ lengths across the wave fronts.

charts.name: Regular
domains: T^2 - Z^2 \le X^2 + Y^2 \;\text{(behind both wave fronts)}

parameters.description: Strength of the wave that crosses $u = 0$, an inverse length
Strength of the wave that crosses $v = 0$, an inverse length; $1/\sqrt{2ab}$ is the radius of both factors of the product AdS$_2 \times$ S$^2$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(T, Z, X, Y)$, all dimensionless. With $\xi = au + bv$, $\eta = bv - au$, and $k = \sqrt{2ab}$ they are $T = -\cos\xi\cosh ky$, $Z = \cos\xi\sinh ky$, $X = \cos\eta\cos kx$, and $Y = \cos\eta\sin kx$, one to one for $-\pi < kx \le \pi$ on either side of $\eta = 0$.
charts.line_element: ds^2 = \dfrac{-\left(1 + Z^2\right)dT^2 + 2TZ\,dT\,dZ + \left(1 - T^2\right)dZ^2}{2ab\left(1 - T^2 + Z^2\right)} + \dfrac{\left(1 - Y^2\right)dX^2 + 2XY\,dX\,dY + \left(1 - X^2\right)dY^2}{2ab\left(1 - X^2 - Y^2\right)}

charts.name: Global

parameters.description: Strength of the wave that crosses $u = 0$, an inverse length
Strength of the wave that crosses $v = 0$, an inverse length; $1/\sqrt{2ab}$ is the radius of both factors of the product AdS$_2 \times$ S$^2$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(\chi, \rho, \theta, \phi)$, all dimensionless. With $\xi = au + bv$ and $k = \sqrt{2ab}$ they are $\sinh\rho = \cos\xi\sinh ky$, $\sin\chi = -\cos\xi\cosh ky/\cosh\rho$, $\theta = \pi/2 + au - bv$, and $\phi = kx$, and $\phi$ runs over the whole line.

charts.name: Kruskal-Szekeres

parameters.description: Strength of the wave that crosses $u = 0$, an inverse length
Strength of the wave that crosses $v = 0$, an inverse length; $1/\sqrt{2ab}$ is the radius of both factors of the product AdS$_2 \times$ S$^2$

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(U, V, \eta, x)$, with $U$, $V$, and $x$ lengths and $\eta = bv - au$ dimensionless. With $q = 1/\sqrt{2ab}$ and $\xi = au + bv$, the null coordinates are $U = -q\,e^{y/q}\cos\xi/(1 + \sin\xi)$ and $V = -q\,e^{-y/q}\cos\xi/(1 + \sin\xi)$, so $2abUV = (1 - \sin\xi)/(1 + \sin\xi)$.

charts.name: Bertotti-Robinson

parameters.description: Strength of the wave that crosses $u = 0$, an inverse length
Strength of the wave that crosses $v = 0$, an inverse length; $1/\sqrt{2ab}$ is the radius of both factors of the product AdS$_2 \times$ S$^2$, the $b$ of the Bertotti-Robinson universe

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, all dimensionless. With $q = 1/\sqrt{2ab}$ they are $t = e^{y/q}\tan(au + bv)$, $r = e^{y/q}\sec(au + bv)$, $\theta = \pi/2 + au - bv$, and $\phi = x/q$, and $\phi$ runs over the whole line.

spacetimes.name: Bertotti-Robinson Electrovacuum
spacetimes.description: A conformally flat electrovacuum solution with uniform electromagnetic field, geometrically the product of two spaces of two dimensions each (AdS₂ × S²). It appears as the limit near the horizon of an extremal Reissner-Nordström black hole.
spacetimes.convention: We keep factors of $c$ and $G$ explicit. The single parameter $b$ is the common radius of the two factors, and every sphere of the spacetime has the areal radius $b$. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.

related.text: The charged black hole. With its charge at the largest value that keeps a horizon, the limit of its geometry toward that horizon is the Bertotti-Robinson solution [gibbons1993].
Any number of extremal charged black holes at rest. The limit toward the horizon of each is a Bertotti-Robinson throat, however many of them stand together.
The time and radial directions of Bertotti-Robinson form an anti-de Sitter space of two dimensions with radius $b$.
The product of de Sitter space of two dimensions and a sphere of the same radius, a vacuum with a positive cosmological constant and no field [nariai1950, krasinski1999].
Tullio Levi-Civita found the Bertotti-Robinson geometry in 1917, two years before his static cylinder [levicivita1917, levicivita1919].
The other universe held together by its own electromagnetic field, a bundle of magnetic field lines along an axis [bonnor1954, melvin1964].

Two plane electromagnetic shock waves that collide head on leave this geometry between their fronts, with $b = 1/\sqrt{2ab}$ set by the strengths $a$ and $b$ of the two waves. It lasts as far as the Killing-Cauchy horizon where the waves focus each other [bell1974, griffiths1991].

The charged black hole in de Sitter space. The limit toward the horizon of its cold member is a product of a two dimensional spacetime and a sphere, and at $\Lambda = 0$ that product is Bertotti and Robinson's [romans1992].
The throat of an extreme black hole that spins, a vacuum with a circle twisted over the anti-de Sitter factor at every polar angle [bardeen1999].

The rotating black hole has a throat of its own. James Bardeen and Gary Horowitz took the limit toward the horizon of an extreme Kerr hole in 1999 and found a vacuum solution with many of the properties of AdS$_2 \times$ S$^2$ [bardeen1999].

Balls of Yang-Mills field with a regular centre, one for each number $n$ of zeros of the field. In the limit $n \to \infty$ the metric at the edge of their core tends to AdS$_2 \times$ S$^2$ [breitenlohner1994].
A pair of extremal black holes with opposite magnetic charges. Each of its poles opens into a throat, which is Bertotti and Robinson's universe once an outside field balances the pair [emparan2000].

charts.name: Static throat

parameters.description: Common radius of the two factors, a length; it is fixed by the field through $b^2 = \dfrac{c^4}{8\pi G u}$, where $u$ is the energy density of the uniform electromagnetic field, and it equals the charge radius $r_q$ of the extremal Reissner-Nordstrom hole whose throat this is

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ a time and $r$ a length along the AdS$_2$ factor. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

charts.name: Poincaré

parameters.description: Common radius of the two factors, a length; it is fixed by the field through $b^2 = \dfrac{c^4}{8\pi G u}$, where $u$ is the energy density of the uniform electromagnetic field, and it equals the charge radius $r_q$ of the extremal Reissner-Nordstrom hole whose throat this is

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ a time and $x$ a length along the AdS$_2$ factor, related to the static chart by $rx = b^2$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

spacetimes.name: Bianchi Anisotropic Cosmologies
spacetimes.description: A family of spatially homogeneous but generally anisotropic cosmologies classified by the symmetry group of their spatial slices. They generalize FLRW models to study anisotropy in the early universe.
spacetimes.convention: We keep factors of $c$ and $G$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.

related.text: The isotropic case, with one scale factor in place of three. Types I and VII$_0$ hold the flat universe, V and VII$_h$ the open one, and IX the closed one [ellismaccallum1969].
The vacuum of type I, two axes stretching and one squeezing at fixed exponents [kasner1921].
Type IX in vacuum, which Charles Misner named in 1969 after a kitchen mixer [misner1969].
Abraham Taub's vacuum of 1951 is type IX with two axes equal, and it extends through a horizon into the NUT region [taub1951, misner1963].
The homogeneous cosmologies outside Bianchi's classification, with space $\mathbb{R} \times S^2$ [kantowski1966, ellismaccallum1969].

Where the expanding Bianchi universes end up when the cosmological constant is positive. Robert Wald proved in 1983 that every type but IX approaches de Sitter space exponentially, and that type IX does too when $\Lambda$ is large enough [wald1983].

charts.name: Type I, Cartesian

parameters.description: Scale factor along $x$ ($a_1 > 0$), dimensionless
Scale factor along $y$ ($a_2 > 0$), dimensionless
Scale factor along $z$ ($a_3 > 0$); the three are independent, and the model is isotropic only where they agree

charts.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, with $t$ a cosmic time and $x$, $y$, and $z$ comoving Cartesian lengths, and the three scale factors $a_1(t)$, $a_2(t)$, and $a_3(t)$ are arbitrary, positive, and dimensionless. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a prime is the derivative with respect to that chart time, $a_i' = \dfrac{da_i}{d(ct)} = \dfrac{1}{c}\dfrac{da_i}{dt}$ and $a_i'' = \dfrac{1}{c^2}\dfrac{d^2a_i}{dt^2}$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

spacetimes.name: Black Saturn
spacetimes.description: A black ring turning in balance around a spherical black hole in five dimensions, the exact vacuum solution Henriette Elvang and Pau Figueras built in 2007 by the inverse scattering method. Rotation alone holds the two apart, each drags the other around, and one mass and angular momentum can be shared between them in a continuum of ways.
spacetimes.convention: The spacetime has five dimensions, with $G$ Newton's constant there. We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.

related.text: Black Saturn with its ring taken away. In the limit $\kappa_3 \to \kappa_2$ and then $\kappa_2 \to 0$ the ring's horizon shrinks to nothing and leaves the Myers-Perry black hole with one spin [elvang2007].

The static black hole of five dimensions. A Saturn whose hole turns against its ring can have the same mass and no angular momentum at infinity, so those two numbers do not single it out [elvang2007].
A thin black ring is a black string bent into a circle and set spinning. It is expected to share the string's Gregory-Laflamme instability [elvang2006, elvang2007].
Black holes held apart by electric charge, in four dimensions. Saturn's ring and hole carry no charge, and rotation does the holding [elvang2007].

Dimensionless, with $0 < \kappa_3 \le \kappa_2 < \kappa_1 \le 1$: on the axis $\rho = 0$ the horizon of the hole is $\kappa_1 \le z \le 1$, and $\kappa_1 = 1$ leaves the ring alone
Dimensionless: on the axis the horizon of the ring is $\kappa_3 \le z \le \kappa_2$, and $\kappa_2 < z < \kappa_1$ is the plane of the ring between the ring and the hole
Dimensionless: on the axis $z < \kappa_3$ is the plane of the ring outside the ring

Dimensionless, the $\bar c_2$ of Elvang and Figueras: the hole's own angular momentum, which vanishes at $\beta = 0$. The ring and the hole are in balance, with no conical membrane between them, where $\left(1 + \kappa_2\beta\right)^2 = \dfrac{\left(\kappa_1 - \kappa_2\right)^2}{\kappa_1\left(1 - \kappa_2\right)\left(1 - \kappa_3\right)\left(\kappa_1 - \kappa_3\right)}$
The parameter of the soliton that sets the ring turning, in units of $L$; at this value the metric is smooth across $\rho = 0$, $z = 0$
The parameter of the soliton that sets the hole turning, in units of $L$
Shift of $t$ along $\psi$, in units of $L$, with which $g_{t\psi}$ vanishes at infinity
Constant with which $g_{\rho\rho}$ at infinity is flat space's and the circles of $\psi$ and $\phi$ close smoothly with the period $2\pi$
Weyl's $\rho$ in units of $L^2$
Weyl's $z$ in units of $L^2$, measured from the rod end where the seed's rod of negative density began
Soliton of the rod end $z = 0$, where the seed's rod of negative density began
Soliton of the rod end $z = 1$, where the hole's horizon meets the plane across the ring's
Soliton of the rod end $z = \kappa_1$, where the hole's horizon meets the plane of the ring
Soliton of the rod end $z = \kappa_2$, the inner edge of the ring
Soliton of the rod end $z = \kappa_3$, the outer edge of the ring
Distance from the rod end $z = 0$ in the flat half plane of $\rho$ and $z$
Distance from the rod end $z = 1$ in that half plane
The seed's part of $H_x$, the static ring and hole
The part of $H_x$ that the ring's rotation adds
The part of $H_x$ that the hole's rotation adds
The part of $H_x$ linear in each rotation
The part of $H_x$ quadratic in each rotation
Common denominator of $H_x$, $H_y$, and $\omega_\psi$
Elvang and Figueras's $H_x$
Elvang and Figueras's $H_y$, with $g_{tt} = -H_y/H_x$, so it vanishes on the ergosurfaces
Elvang and Figueras's $G_y$ in units of $L^2$, the part of the metric the solitons leave as the seed had it
Elvang and Figueras's $P$
Elvang and Figueras's $\omega_\psi$ in units of $L$, with $g_{t\psi} = -L\left(\omega_\psi + qH_y\right)/H_x$

Dimensionless function: $L\,e^{V}$ is the radius of the circle of $\psi$ through a point. For black Saturn $e^{2V} = \dfrac{G_yH_x^2 - \left(\omega_\psi + qH_y\right)^2}{H_xH_y}$, as a function of $r$ and $\theta$ through $\rho$ and $z$

Dimensionless function: $c\,\Omega/L$ is the angular velocity about the hole, seen from infinity, of an observer with no angular momentum, the dragging of frames. For black Saturn $\Omega = \dfrac{\omega_\psi + qH_y}{H_x}e^{-2V}$, as a function of $r$ and $\theta$ through $\rho$ and $z$

Dimensionless function: $L^2\rho\,e^{V - W}$ is the area of the torus of $\psi$ and $\phi$ through a point over $4\pi^2$. For black Saturn $e^{2W} = G_y$, as a function of $r$ and $\theta$ through $\rho$ and $z$
Dimensionless function, the conformal factor of the half plane of $\rho$ and $z$. For black Saturn $e^{2\nu} = k^2H_xP$, as a function of $r$ and $\theta$ through $\rho$ and $z$

charts.convention: We use the polar coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \psi, \phi)$ of Elvang and Figueras, with $r$ a length, in which flat space is $-c^2dt^2 + dr^2 + r^2d\theta^2 + r^2\sin^2\theta\,d\psi^2 + r^2\cos^2\theta\,d\phi^2$. The functions $V$, $\Omega$, $W$, and $\nu$ are those of Weyl's chart and stand free in every component. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, so $\dot{t}$ in the geodesic equations means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
